title: Customer Fidelity Credit Portability Framework
author: Maya Chen
content:
Purpose and scope

This document describes the Customer Fidelity Credit Portability Framework: the rules, primitives, and operational playbooks that allow customers to transfer, convert, or reconcile fidelity credits (promotional, escrowed, or purchased) between Redwood deployment surfaces (Hosted API, Dedicated, Private) and across billing constructs. The framework targets commerce and product teams, billing engineers, and solutions engineers enabling predictable customer migrations and minimal friction for enterprise transitions.

Goals

- Reduce friction for customers migrating workloads between Hosted, Dedicated, and Private by providing predictable credit handling.
- Ensure correct accounting and minimal financial exposure for Redwood.
- Provide deterministic UX and API primitives for credit visibility, conversion, and rollback.
- Minimize manual billing operations and exception cases.

Non-goals

- This doc does not replace contract-level legal terms for enterprise discounts or bespoke financial instruments.
- It does not define new pricing tiers; it defines mapping and operational rules for credit portability only.

Definitions and primitives

- Fidelity Credit: A unit representing monetary or usage value issued to a customer that can be applied toward Redwood consumption. Types: Promotional, Escrowed, Purchased, Insurance Credits.
- Portability: Movement of credit value between account constructs (e.g., hosted account -> dedicated tenant) without changing the underlying monetary backing unless conversion occurs.
- Conversion Rate: A deterministic multiplier used when mapping credit value across different pricing surfaces to reflect differing unit economics (e.g., hosted per-token price vs dedicated reserved capacity).
- Escrow Bucket: Temporary holding state for credits pending migration, approval, or reconciliation.

High-level portability modes

1) Direct Pass-through
   - Credits remain denominated in Redwood currency and are moved 1:1 between account constructs.
   - Use-case: Small customers moving between hosted sub-accounts under the same billing entity.
   - Constraints: Only allowed when pricing tiers and entitlement structures match.

2) Conversion-on-Move
   - Credits are converted using an agreed conversion rate at the time of migration.
   - Use-case: Hosted (per-token) credits converted to Dedicated capacity credits or vice versa.
   - Conversion is timestamped and recorded for audit.

3) Escrow-with-Approval
   - Credits are placed in an Escrow Bucket pending finance approval when policy or contract deviations are detected.
   - Use-case: Customer with promotional credits tied to Hosted wants to move to Private where legal/compliance prevents full pass-through.

Conversion model and formulas

- Conversion must be deterministic. The canonical conversion formula: converted_value = original_value * conversion_multiplier - conversion_fee
- Conversion multiplier is determined by lookup table (managed in Pricing Catalog service) keyed by (from_surface, to_surface, date).
- Conversion_fee is applied only when the portability causes a measurable economic delta (e.g., converting promotional credits into committed capacity).

Pricing catalog sample (table)

From | To | Multiplier | Fee 
-----|----|------------|-----
Hosted (per-token) | Dedicated (reserved credits) | 0.85 | $0.00 (applied by default)
Hosted | Private (on-prem credit) | 0.70 | $0.00 (requires legal approval)
Purchased bundle | Hosted | 1.00 | $0.00
Escrowed promotional | Any | variable | subject to approval

(Notes: Applied multipliers are reviewed quarterly by Pricing Ops; fees may be negotiated for large enterprise transfers.)

Audit and accounting guarantees

- Every portability transaction creates a signed ledger entry with fields: transaction_id, customer_id, source_bucket, destination_bucket, original_amount, conversion_multiplier, converted_amount, operator_id, timestamp, and policy_id.
- Ledger entries are immutable and stored for minimum 7 years per finance policy.

Customer UX and API primitives

- Console flow: "Migrate credits" modal available on Billing -> Credits page for eligible accounts. Steps: 1) Select source bucket, 2) Select destination surface, 3) Preview conversion (shows multiplier, fees), 4) Acknowledge terms, 5) Initiate migration.
- API: POST /v1/billing/credits/migrate {source_bucket_id, destination_surface, amount, metadata} -> returns migration_preview_id and estimated_conversion. POST /v1/billing/credits/migrate/confirm {migration_preview_id} -> executes migration.
- Webhooks: credit_migration.requested, credit_migration.completed, credit_migration.rejected.

Operational playbooks

1) Self-serve migration (automated)
   - Preconditions: customer has single billing entity, no security/legal constraints, conversion multiplier defined, projected converted_amount <= $250k.
   - Steps: 1) Customer initiates via console or API; 2) System validates entitlements and pricing mappings; 3) System executes conversion and emits webhooks; 4) Customer receives final invoice adjustment if needed.

2) Escrow and manual approval
   - Preconditions: cross-entity move, legal constraints, high-value (> $250k), or promotional credits flagged as non-portable.
   - Steps: 1) Credits moved into Escrow Bucket with status=PENDING_APPROVAL; 2) Notifications to Finance and Legal; 3) Review with customer; 4) Approve -> execute conversion or Reject -> return credits to origin with audit note.

3) Rollback and dispute handling
   - If a post-migration reconciliation detects a mismatch, the system supports: automatic rollback (if within 72 hours and destination usage < 10% of migrated credits) or dispute workflow (Finance case created, customer credited pending resolution).

Edge cases and guardrails

- Multi-tenant mappings: Individual sub-account credits cannot be ported across top-level billing accounts without written authorization.
- Time-bounded promos: Promotional credits with expiry shorter than 90 days are non-portable by default.
- Negative balance protection: Conversion cannot create negative reserved capacity entitlements. Any residual shortfall triggers an invoice event.
- Tax and regulatory: Movement of credits that change tax treatment require Finance sign-off; Private/on-prem transfers typically require additional compliance checks.

Telemetry and observability

Instrument all migration flows with the following metrics: credit_migration_attempts, credit_migration_success, credit_migration_fail_reason, average_conversion_multiplier, escrow_pending_count. Provide per-customer logs and an aggregated weekly dashboard in Redwood Console (Billing -> Credit Portability).

Policies and approval matrix

- Auto-approve threshold: <= $250k and same billing entity.
- Finance review threshold: > $250k and <= $2M.
- Executive/Legal review: > $2M or cross-jurisdiction movement to Private/on-prem.

Implementation plan and milestones (Q4 2026 -> Q1 2027)

1) Q4 2026 (Pilot)
   - Implement conversion catalog and immutable ledger.
   - Expose API preview endpoint and console migration modal (alpha).
   - Run pilot with 3 enterprise customers migrating Hosted->Dedicated.
2) Q1 2027 (General availability)
   - Add escrow approval workflow, notification plumbing (Slack + email), and webhooks.
   - Integrate with billing engine and reconciliation jobs.
3) Q2 2027 (Scale & compliance)
   - Support Private/on-prem transfers with legal workflow templates and multi-jurisdiction tax handling.

Rollout checklist for launch

- [ ] Conversion catalog seeded for top 10 SKUs.
- [ ] Console preview + confirm modal QAed and accessibility tested.
- [ ] API contract versioned and documented in developer docs.
- [ ] Escrow notification runbook created and routed to Finance and Legal channels.
- [ ] Audit retention storage provisioned and encryption validated.

Open questions and decision points

- Should conversion multipliers decay over time to reflect pricing changes, or remain snapshot-based at migration time? Recommended: snapshot-based with clear timestamps.
- What is the appropriate commercial rebate (if any) for customers who initiated migration within 30 days of a major pricing change? Finance to propose a template.

Appendix: Example migration transcript (Hosted -> Dedicated)

1) Customer requests migration of $100,000 hosted credits to Dedicated.
2) Pricing catalog multiplier for date 2026-11-01 is 0.85. Estimated converted credits = $85,000 equivalent reserved capacity.
3) System creates ledger entry TX-20261101-0001, moves funds, emits webhooks.
4) Customer consumes Dedicated capacity; monthly reconciler validates usage and final invoice adjusts for residual rounding differences.
